title: Diagnostic stream boundary
description: A failure is reported on the error stream and never on the data stream. Three of Tinman's commands write output another program reads, the JSON model, the manual page and the completion script, so stdout is a data stream rather than a place to talk to the operator, and a diagnostic written there lands in the middle of whatever the consumer is parsing. Discharged by the reference-boundary checker in verification support, which scans the implementation tree for the forbidden expressions and reports any occurrence. Attested by the @contract scenario in features/command-surface.feature.
rationale: Four paths printed a failure to stdout. Three were found by reading a Rule that named them, given a scenario each, and fixed; the fourth sat in the inspect --examples arms and was invisible to all three, because a scenario proves its own path and says nothing about the path beside it. A bound over the tree is what reaches a command added later that nobody remembers to cover. Known weakness, stated so a reader does not over-trust a green: this keys on the project's current failure-reporting idiom, the interpolated binding named failure, so a diagnostic printed by another spelling is invisible to it. That is the limit a text-matched reference boundary always carries, and closing it needs a checker reading syntax rather than text. The doubles check met the same limit from the other side and left the rule set for a step definition on 2026-07-31, because reading a mark's content is beyond what a rule can match; this contract stays a rule because the token it forbids is a spelling rather than a meaning.
